stage: round-1 fix stage (group G7), 18 Oct 2026; drafted by Claude (Anthropic), pending team review
cell: Keeps combine|filter|mix|resample|tone (test); cluster_id chain:combine|filter|mix|resample|tone. Its former dev twin gbf-dev-06 was re-themed (SSB, cell combine|filter|hilbert|mix|resample|tone).

accepted.change: The beacon is now keyed by a 5 Hz square-wave Signal Source (off 100 ms, on 100 ms) through Float To Complex and a Multiply. It is not a Vector Source: per fix_plan, that would add data_source and move the cell to dev. The keying is stated in the instruction. V6 now checks the keyed levels in both outputs, all p2p because they hold in the start graph. There are two on-windows and two off-windows of 400 items each, at least 400 items from each keying edge. Channel: rms 0.5 +-5 % while on, <= 0.025 while off. Audio: rms 0.566 +-5 % and peak 0.8 +-5 % while on, <= 0.0283 while off. The 'low-pass filtered' requirement is a p2p graph check: a path Signal Source -> filter block -> File Sink. Its id list holds every GNU Radio 3.10 block that can low-pass filter a channel. The reviewers' graphs, rerun against the final task.json, all fail V6: a free-running 700 Hz oscillator on audio.dat with the faulty BFO kept (off-window rms 0.567); neighbours zeroed with the filter replaced by Keep 1 in N (no filter path); two oscillators straight into the two File Sinks (off windows, no filter path). A graph that rebuilds the keyed tone from its own oscillator times a copy of the key still passes; this is review.notes limit (1).

Resolved by signature v2, a sorted set of the functional classes of all enabled blocks: no path walk and no dependence on connection order. The reference, start.grc and all 12 variants have the signature combine|filter|mix|resample|tone -> test, including v1 (Rotator BFO), which mapped to train under v1. The keying square wave on the Multiply's port 1 is absorbed as an oscillator (verified: on port 0 it would add harmonic_wave, which also hashes to test). build.py asserts the split and prints every signature.

review.notes records that this is a composed L2 graph, used instead of the brief's seed qt-gui/qtgui_multi_input.grc (single-rate, so it has no place for a rate fault). The team must approve composed L2 as a source category and settle the licence (fix_plan team_decisions).

The disjointness line now names t05_qam_debug (QAM demo with sample-rate/type mismatches) and t12_fivegnalizer_modify (FFT-rate bottleneck), next to t20, t17 and t03. It also names the GRC-Agent scenario 22_fm_rx_filter_squelch, which adds a channel filter to an FM receiver. None of them is a CW/BFO receiver or a post-decimation oscillator rate fault.

Same fix as compliance/F1, using the suggested per-window rms checks. The suggested 'replace the BFO and audio path with a free-running 700 Hz oscillator' mutant cannot be written as one edit of the reference: there is no 700 Hz source to rewire from. Its behaviour, a 700 Hz tone that is never silent, is covered by the new 'key held on' mutant (key waveform constant). A second new mutant keys at 10 Hz. Both are killed by the off-window checks, and the oscillator graph itself was probed (see compliance/F1).

The instruction ends with the set run sentence ('The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.'). spec_properties records it as the V5 liveness condition: 8400 items at both points.
Same as compliance/F4: t05_qam_debug and t12_fivegnalizer_modify are named in disjointness.

The channel-filter id list was extended to every GNU Radio 3.10 block that can low-pass filter: added FFT Low Pass Filter, Interpolating FIR, PFB Arbitrary Resampler, the hierarchical channelizer and Integrate. New variant v12 replaces the Low Pass Filter with a decimating FFT Filter. All 11 reviewer and authoring variants are kept: 3 full rebuilds, plus the BFO repaired as a literal 12000, freq -6400 at 96 kHz, BFO -2200 Hz, a new audio_rate variable, an added Throttle, an added audio LPF, a two-branch BFO at 96 kHz, and a Frequency Xlating FIR as the BFO. All 12 variants pass V6. Probes: a Rational Resampler or PFB arbitrary resampler with default taps as the channel filter fails V6, correctly. Their anti-alias band lets the +5.5 kHz neighbour through, so the stated neighbour suppression is not met.

review.notes lists the known limits. (1) The recording is generated inside the editable graph: input tampering, and rebuilding the keyed tone from a copy of the key, are not detected. (2) The level windows tolerate channel-filter delays up to about 33 ms. (3) The filter graph check accepts any listed block; filter quality is left to the signal checks. It also notes the L2 block count (15).
